warnings: Evidence gaps: Weak evidence on Customer Retention - diagnosis confidence limited; Critical gap: No evidence on Operational Efficiency; Critical gap: No evidence on Quality Delivery

Causal adjudication: re-ranked to gtm_channel_mismatch over surface unit_economics_failure — Negative blended unit economics are driven by a channel/go-to-market mismatch (one channel dragging the blend), an upstream cause the engine cannot diagnose.

decisionMemo.businessProblem: Per-customer economics look broken and the team wants to cut product cost, but the loss is concentrated in one place.

rootCauseDiagnosis.description: Go-to-market / channel mismatch: spend concentrated in an underperforming acquisition channel
rootCauseDiagnosis.mechanismDescription: Acquisition is concentrated in a channel with poor conversion or punitive CAC; the issue is channel allocation, not the product or blended economics.
alternativeExplanations: A short-term channel-pricing fluctuation rather than a structural mismatch
An attribution gap masking a profitable channel

intervention.title: Run a channel attribution and channel-level CAC/payback analysis
intervention.objective: Quantify channel-level economics before any budget reallocation
intervention.rationale: Channel attribution and channel-level CAC analysis are analysis-only and reversible; they avoid blindly scaling or cutting a channel.
intervention.whyThisNow: Spend is concentrated in an underperforming channel; channel economics must be measured before reallocation

steps.title: Run a channel attribution analysis
steps.description: Attribute acquisition and conversion by channel to isolate the underperforming channel.

steps.title: Run a channel-level CAC/payback review
steps.description: Compute CAC and payback by channel to size a reversible reallocation toward profitable channels.
steps.successCriteria: Channel-level CAC/payback computed and a reversible reallocation drafted

failureRisks: Channel attribution may be noisy with overlapping touchpoints
intervention.fallbackPlan: Shift a small test budget to the candidate channel and measure before full reallocation

factors.rationale: Expected revenue impact: MINOR. Urgency: HIGH
Duration: 7 days. Team capacity: MEDIUM. Cost: LOW
Failure risks: 1. Fallback plan available: Yes
Cost band: LOW vs Expected impact: MINOR

recommendedInterventions.sequencingReason: Quick implementation builds momentum and shows progress

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually

limitations: Evidence gaps limit precision: Weak evidence on Customer Retention - diagnosis confidence limited; Critical gap: No evidence on Operational Efficiency; Critical gap: No evidence on Quality Delivery
Evidence coverage is insufficient across business dimensions. Deeper investigation recommended before diagnosis finalization.
nextReviewTriggers: After first intervention completion: validate assumptions, collect outcome data
Monthly: Track KPIs (repeat customer rate, turnaround time, complaint count)
If revenue does not improve by 20% within 60 days: pivot to alternative diagnosis
If team capacity exhausted: pause non-critical interventions
If external market changes significantly: reassess competitive positioning
